title: form::Field::editable linked its guard by a name the guard never had -- the guard exists, the link was dead
body:
`form::Field::editable`'s doc linked a guard by a name the guard never had. **The guard itself has existed since `771cc847` (2026-08-30), introduced in the SAME COMMIT as the dead link.** The remedy was a link repair, landed at `2d3228c6`.

## SUPERSEDED -- the original claim, kept because the error is the point

> `form::Field::editable`'s doc names a guard that does not exist, and the guard is the one thing standing between a form declaration and an edit the store refuses. [...] `offers_an_edit_the_surface_refuses` appears **exactly once in the whole tree: in that doc comment.** It is an intra-doc link to a method that was never written. `impl Loaded` carries `load` and `from_str` and nothing else.

**The last sentence was false when it was written.** `impl Loaded` carried, and had carried for three days, `load`, `from_str`, `forms`, `widgets`, `form`, `changeable_and_not_on_any_form` and `offers_an_edit_that_cannot_land`.

## What is actually there

`Loaded::offers_an_edit_that_cannot_land` is the guard the comment describes, and it is better than the comment claims:

- It audits `Reach::Never | Reach::NotYet` over the fields a form declares `editable`, which is exactly *offers an edit the surface refuses*.
- It has a **mirror**, `changeable_and_not_on_any_form`, catching the other direction -- a writable field on no form, which the module doc notes is the half that rots silently.
- Both run through **one** `audit` traversal, because two near-identical loops over one population is how two answers drift apart.
- It is covered, with a **non-vacuity control**: `no_row_offers_an_edit_that_cannot_land_and_the_check_is_not_vacuous`.

## The instrument, which is the transferable part

**I measured that the LINK NAME appears once in the tree, and inferred from that the MECHANISM was absent.** A search on a name cannot see a mechanism under a different name, so the inference does not follow -- and nothing about the output said so, because the grep was correct about the only question it was asked.

**This is the second time in one day the same instrument misled me.** The first reported `Op::Graphql` ABSENT because a grep for `fn|struct|enum <name>` cannot see an enum VARIANT; that one was caught only because the name had been planted as a positive control and the control failed.

**The general form: a name census answers a question about NAMES. Promoting it to a claim about MECHANISMS needs a second step nobody performed -- reading the site that would hold the mechanism.**

## The population, RE-DRIVEN, because my split of it was wrong in the same way

I recorded six rustdoc targets as *absent from the code entirely*, against a remainder that merely link to items that exist. **Re-driven against the sites rather than the names, five of the six are present under another name or path:**

| cited target            | truth                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `offers_an_edit_the_surface_refuses` | `Loaded::offers_an_edit_that_cannot_land` -- this issue          |
| `ingest::from_md`       | `Facade::ingest_from_md`                                                     |
| `Store::apply_changes`  | `Store::commit_mutation`                                                     |
| `reserved_is_free`      | the test `no_declared_entity_kind_is_reserved`                               |
| `AcScope`               | no type of that name; the prose describes a projection, and GraphQL is out of 3.0.1 |
| `AcScopeView`           | same                                                                         |

**So the class is overwhelmingly one-token path repairs over things that exist, not missing mechanisms** -- and that is the opposite of what my split said. `Facade::put`, `Facade::schema`, `Plan::apply`, `Registry`, `Sigil::accepts` and `Op::Graphql` all name items the crate really has and merely cannot reach by rustdoc's path rules from where the link sits.

**It changes the size of the doc gate's flip condition, which is why it is recorded here rather than only in a board.** The condition is *when the unresolved class is gone*; if the class were mostly absent mechanisms it would be a build, and it is not.

## Reach

`AcScope` and `AcScopeView` are NOT resolved by this issue. They are the only two of the six with no present-day referent, they sit in `graphql.rs`, and GraphQL mutations are out of 3.0.1 by ruling -- so whether that prose is corrected or removed is not this issue's to take.
